title: [Runner] Fix false-positive Win+Shift+C shortcut conflict on Windows 11

confidence.rationale: Exact current test returns without assertions on Windows 10; the production OS guard itself is correct and is not alleged to fail.

proposed_comments.body:
### Make the OS-specific bypass coverage explicit and deterministic

**Severity:** `low` (non-blocking test coverage)

**Affected code:** `src/runner/UnitTests/HotkeyConflictTests.cpp`, `HasConflict_LegacyWinShiftC_OnWindows11_NoConflict`, and the Windows-version bypass in `src/runner/hotkey_conflict_detector.cpp`.

**Problem:** On Windows 10 the test returns without an assertion, so a passing result does not mean the OS-specific bypass was checked. On Windows 11 it exercises the real manager, but it does not check the Windows 10 decision.

**Why it matters:** The production exception is deliberately Windows-11-specific. Explicit coverage of both decisions would protect that boundary without depending on which Windows version the test machine runs. This is a coverage improvement, not a claim that the current production predicate is wrong.

**Suggested change:**

1. Factor the small bypass predicate into a testable helper taking the hotkey and a Windows-11-or-greater Boolean; have production supply the actual OS result.
2. Test that Win+Shift+C bypasses only when that Boolean is true, and that another chord does not bypass.
3. Keep the existing real-manager integration check separately; if it is restricted to Windows 11, report the other OS as inconclusive rather than returning a successful test. Do not assert that every Windows 10 machine must fail `RegisterHotKey`, since that depends on the environment.

**Verification:** Run the focused `HotkeyConflictTests` after the change. The pure predicate cases should exercise both OS decisions on the same host; the integration result should explicitly distinguish an executed assertion from an unsupported-OS skip.
proposed_comments.out_of_diff_reason: The deterministic coverage remedy coordinates the production bypass predicate and its integration/unit tests; this general implementation request avoids presenting an uncompiled multi-location patch.
proposed_comments.title: Make the OS-specific bypass coverage explicit and deterministic
